title: Hybrid hosting recommendation workbook
body:
Purpose:
This workbook is a practical decision aid for customer POCs where a hybrid mixing of hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes is under consideration. Use this to quickly surface the dominant constraints (latency, data sensitivity, cost), map them to architectural levers, and produce a recommended starting topology plus a low-effort canary plan.

Context / customer snapshot (fill in per-customer):
- industry: Retail (sample)
- expected peak QPS: 120 requests/sec (write in actual)
- median tokens/request: 350 tokens
- 95th pct latency target: 300ms server-side
- data sensitivity: PII in user messages (regulated)
- network topology: multi-region read-heavy, writes centralized
- procurement constraints: prefers monthly reserved capacity for predictability

Quick recommendation summary (example):
- Short answer: Hybrid-primary-hosted with Dedicated-warmed-reserve AND Private-VPC for regulated batch jobs.
  - Hosted API (primary): day-to-day inference for >90% of traffic to get quick time-to-value, streaming responses, and experimentability.
  - Dedicated (reserve pool): autoscaled GPU pool for peak capacity + deterministic tail latencies; serves heavy batch, low-latency customer-facing routes, and handles burst isolation.
  - Private VPC (air-gapped style): for regulated bulk processing / audit workflows; replicated model versions but with reduced scale initially.

Why this pattern? (decision logic)
- If data must remain in-customer network or goes through regulated pipelines => Private must exist for that workload.
- If predictable latency and isolation are required for some routes (e.g., checkout recommendations) => Dedicated reserved nodes for those routes.
- If we need quick iteration and model switching for low-risk routes => Hosted wins for developer velocity and metrics.

Evaluation matrix (fill per-route):
- Columns to evaluate: route name | target latency | availability SLO | data sensitivity | qps share | burstiness | must-run-on-prem? | recommended mode | notes
- Example row: "recommendations-api | 150ms | 99.95% | PII token-level | 10% | medium bursts | no | dedicated | pin model v1.3 with quantized variant"

Cost sensitivity shorthand (quick calc heuristics):
- baseline assumptions: hosted per-token ~ $0.00006 (sample), Dedicated reserve amortized gpu-hour =~ $3-$8/hr depending on instance and commitment, private infra capital ops vary (one-time + 20% annual ops).
- Rule of thumb: >50M tokens/mo and 95th pct latency <200ms -> strongly prefer dedicated for cost and tail control.
- When data residency adds >20% operational overhead, model-selective private paths for sensitive routes only.

Sizing quick-guide (workbook steps):
1) Convert expected traffic -> tokens/sec: QPS * median_tokens.
2) Estimate tokens/sec throughput per GPU type: e.g., A100-80GB (fp16) approx 3500 tokens/s for our model family; L4s ~700 tokens/s.
3) Dedicated GPU need = ceil(tokens/sec_needed / tokens/s_per_gpu) * headroom (1.3x).
4) Warm/cold: reserve 60-80% of calculated GPUs for base, allow burst to hosted or autoscale with higher-cost instances.

Operational playbook (minimal viable):
- Instrumentation: per-route token counters, tail latency histograms, model-version tagging in traces, and traceroute to region.
- Rollout plan: canary 1% on dedicated -> monitor latency/errors/quality -> 10% -> 100% for that route. For private tasks, ingest-only canary runs before permitting outputs to downstream systems.
- Fallbacks: primary fallback sequence for requests: dedicated -> hosted-fallback-model (compatible smaller variant) -> degraded response with cached summary.

Model and quantization strategy notes:
- Use same model family across modes when possible to simplify fallbacks (e.g., 13B on hosted and dedicated).
- Provide smaller quantized variants for hosted fallback, prioritize consistent tokenizer and special tokens.
- Lockpoint: do not switch tokenization between routes.

Security/compliance checklist (sensitive customers):
- KMS/HSM integration verified for Private and Dedicated key management.
- Audit logging path: all inference inputs/outputs for private flows to customer-controlled S3/Blob with retention policy.
- Data-in-transit: TLS 1.3 mandatory; private network peering for VPC.
- Legal: ensure data processing addendum + SOC/ISO reports aligned with customer compliance.

Common tradeoffs (shorthand):
- Velocity vs Control: Hosted = fastest, least control. Dedicated = medium velocity, strong tail control. Private = slowest to set up, strongest compliance.
- Cost predictability: Dedicated reserved > predictable. Hosted = pay-as-you-go. Private = CapEx + ops.
- Failure modes: Hosted region outage -> route to Dedicated or other region. Dedicated capacity exhaustion -> fallback to hosted (if data policy allows) or degraded responses.

Risk register (quick):
- Risk: Procurement delays for Dedicated. Mitigation: start hosted + simulate load to prove capacity needs, parallel procurement.
- Risk: Onboarding private VPC takes 6+ weeks. Mitigation: parallelize network prep and cert provisioning.
- Risk: Model divergence across variants causes user-visible regressions. Mitigation: shared eval suite and regression alerts tied to prompt sets.

Open questions / customer decisions needed:
- Which routes are strictly "data cannot leave customer boundary"? (list)
- Expected 95th token length distribution (we need p95 tokens/request).
- Acceptance criteria for fallback to hosted for private-sensitive failures.
- Procurement timeline for reserved capacity (target months).

Action items / TODOs for Solutions Eng: (assign owners)
- [Ava] Run a micro-benchmark with customer's sample prompt set to get model tokens/s metrics (due: +3 days).
- [Daniel] Draft Dedicated sizing estimate + cost tiers (due: +5 days).
- [Priya] Create Private-VPC checklist for networking and KMS handoff (due: +7 days).
- [Ethan] Wire up quick eval harness to compare primary model vs quantized fallback (due: +4 days).

Appendix: quick canary config (template)
- Canary route config: traffic_split { primary: 98%, dedicated_canary: 1%, private_canary: 1% }
- SLOs to watch: 95th latency, error rate, token-per-request variance, and quality regression (BLEU/ROUGE or custom prompts).
- Alert thresholds: increase in 95th latency >20% or error rate >0.1% triggers immediate rollback.

Notes to self / working items:
- Keep this doc customer-agnostic but copy into customer folder and populate route-specific rows.
- Link in Confluence: hybrid-guidelines and infra-sizing playbook.
- Reminder: collect customer's compliance rubric and add to ledger before Private kickoff.

Raw scratch area (for quick math):
- sample: 120 qps * 350 tokens = 42k tokens/sec -> tokens/sec * 3600 * 24 * 30 =~ 108M tokens/mo.
- If A100 throughput ~3500 tok/s -> need 42k/3500=12 GPUs -> with 1.3x headroom -> 16 GPUs reserved.
- Monthly cost rough: 16 * $6/hr * 24 * 30 = ~$69,120 (example). Hosted cost estimate for 108M tokens at $0.00006/token = ~$6,480/mo — shows host cost can be lower for small volumes but dedicated becomes better at scale for per-token cost and tail control.

End of workbook. Keep iterations lightweight and flag unknowns early.
